Recommended intervention: Install a differential pressure (DP) transmitter across a bypass of the chiller condenser water inlet and outlet, plus one redundant temperature sensor at the condenser outlet, on both chiller circuits. Use these measurements to compute a real-time condenser thermal resistance baseline. This method directly targets the fouling mechanism (scale buildup reducing heat transfer area) without altering the fixed water chemistry or requiring shutdowns longer than the 48-hour limit, as it is a passive monitoring retrofit.

PARAMETER: Number of chiller circuits instrumented — 2 — ASSUMPTION 
PARAMETER: Monitoring Method — Differential pressure and temperature logging — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.22691356]
PARAMETER: Fouling Indicator — Condenser Thermal Resistance — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Baseline Establishment Period — 14 days of healthy operation — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Action Threshold — Deviation of +3 sigma from baseline thermal resistance — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Target Capacity Loss Prevention — 11% — EVIDENCE-BACKED [user problem statement]
PARAMETER: Target Energy Penalty Reduction — 22% — EVIDENCE-BACKED [user problem statement]

Expected measurable effect: The system will identify the onset of fouling when the calculated condenser thermal resistance exceeds the 3-sigma threshold. This allows operators to schedule cleaning within the 48-hour annual window before the 11% capacity loss and 22% kW/ton penalty occur, rather than reacting to catastrophic failure.

Falsification test:
Test Temperature: 30 C ambient (peak load summer conditions)
Duration: 30 days continuous monitoring post-installation
Sample Size n: 2 chiller circuits
Pass/Fail Criteria: PASS if the system triggers an alarm within 24 hours of a simulated fouling event (introducing a controlled resistance drop) and no false alarms occur during the first 14 days of healthy baseline. FAIL if the system does not detect the simulated event or generates more than one false alarm per month.
